research_goal: Create backend-ready kickboxing knowledge for rule systems and style families: WAKO point fighting, light contact, kick light, full contact, low kick, K1; GLORY/K-1 style; and Muay Thai overlap and differences.

source_refs.title: Understanding Muay Thai Rules and Regulations
source_refs.organization_or_author: International Federation of Muaythai Associations context site
source_refs.notes: Used only as adjacent comparator for Muay Thai legality and tactical differences: elbows, extended clinch, knees, sweeps, ring control, and scoring culture.

key_rules_scoring_incentives: Score clean controlled touches before opponent.
Reset after scoring actions.
Prioritize speed, accuracy, distance, first-step timing, and immediate exit.
Avoid damage-seeking exchanges and prolonged pocket fighting.
technical_implications: Bladed or mobile stance can be useful if balance and exit quality remain intact.
Lead-leg dexterity, blitz entries, feints, and fast recovery outrank attritional low-kick work.
Conditioning should protect speed and reactivity rather than create long fatigue exchanges.

key_rules_scoring_incentives: Continuous fighting with controlled power.
Score through clean technique, volume, balance, defense, and composure.
Excessive force is a rule and safety problem.
technical_implications: Combination flow and guard return are central.
Athlete must defend while striking instead of pausing after single scores.
Aerobic repeatability and movement quality matter more than knockout power.

key_rules_scoring_incentives: Use controlled techniques from low-kick kickboxing.
Balance punching and kicking rather than treating leg kicks as full-power attrition.
Low-kick legality adds stance, checking, and leg-defense scoring relevance.
technical_implications: Stance must support checking and low-kick defense.
Teach low-kick mechanics with strict control before contact volume rises.
Shin, ankle, knee, hip, and adductor load must be progressed gradually.

key_rules_scoring_incentives: Punches and legal above-waist kicks drive scoring.
Continuous ring fighting rewards combination volume, clean impact, and ringcraft.
Low-kick attrition is not the tactical center.
technical_implications: Punch-to-body-or-head-kick combinations are high priority.
Guard endurance, trunk rotation, hip mobility, and round repeatability matter.
Stance can be less low-kick defensive than K1 or low kick, but must still protect balance.

key_rules_scoring_incentives: Legal kicks to the opponent's legs change scoring, damage, stance, and defense.
Leg attacks can score directly and reduce opponent mobility.
Athlete must attack legs without losing posture or eating counters.
technical_implications: Low-kick setup and return defense are mandatory.
Checking, pullbacks, stance width, weight distribution, and lead-leg management are core skills.
Hard low-kick volume requires conservative shin, calf, knee, hip, and adductor progression.

key_rules_scoring_incentives: Blend punches, kicks, and legal knees.
Limited clinch use means knees must be immediate and tactical, not extended wrestling.
Damage, clean impact, ringcraft, and knockdown awareness matter.
technical_implications: Teach punch-kick-knee chains and exits as one system.
Athlete must avoid staying square after kicking or clinch entries.
Anti-clinch posture, frames, immediate knees, and break exits are more relevant than long Muay Thai clinch battles.

key_rules_scoring_incentives: Clean unblocked strikes score; blocked strikes do not carry the same value.
Damage is the primary judging signal.
Aggression, technical cleanness, ring control, and complex techniques influence close rounds.
Knockdowns heavily shape round and fight outcome.
technical_implications: Powerful clean impact matters more than low-effect touch volume.
Kicks, knees, and punches must be defensively responsible because counters and knockdowns dominate outcomes.
Clinch should create immediate legal offense or exit; extended control should not be trained as default.

key_rules_scoring_incentives: Muay Thai allows elbows and deeper clinch work than most kickboxing rule sets.
Knees, kicks, clinch control, sweeps, balance, and visible effect have different value than kickboxing touch or K1 damage models.
Muay Thai clinch dominance should not be assigned to kickboxing unless user context explicitly supports it.
technical_implications: Use Muay Thai as a comparator for knees, clinch posture, checking, and balance.
Do not prescribe elbows, long clinch battles, dumps, or sweep-heavy systems for WAKO/GLORY kickboxing by default.
Kickboxing stance, rhythm, break rules, and scoring incentives usually demand faster exits after clinch or kick contact.

sport_training_rules.rule: Every kickboxing plan must tag rule_set before selecting tactics.
sport_training_rules.then: select from point_fighting, light_contact, kick_light, full_contact, low_kick, k1, glory_k1_style, fitness_kickboxing, or unknown
sport_training_rules.rationale: Scoring, legal targets, contact level, clinch permissions, and conditioning priorities differ by rule system.

sport_training_rules.rule: Unknown rule set defaults to general kickboxing without hard contact assumptions.
sport_training_rules.then: teach stance, guard, footwork, jab_cross, round_kick, basic defense, controlled bag_or_pad work, and technical contact only

sport_training_rules.rule: Point fighting plans prioritize speed, timing, first score, and exit quality.
sport_training_rules.then: use short high-speed entries, lead-leg touch drills, reaction work, feints, and reset scenarios

sport_training_rules.rule: Light contact plans must preserve control and technique during continuous exchanges.
sport_training_rules.then: program combination flow, guard return, defense while striking, aerobic repeatability, and controlled sparring intensity

sport_training_rules.rule: Kick light includes low-kick logic but keeps contact controlled.
sport_training_rules.then: add low-kick targeting, checking, stance discipline, and shin_ankle_adductor load progression

sport_training_rules.rule: Full contact plans bias above-waist kick and punch combinations.
sport_training_rules.then: prioritize punch_to_body_or_head_kick, ringcraft, guard endurance, scoring volume, and round repeatability

sport_training_rules.rule: Low-kick profiles require recurring leg attack and leg defense content.
sport_training_rules.then: include low_kick_setup, check, step_out, pullback, return_defense, stance_width, and lead_leg_management

sport_training_rules.rule: K1 and GLORY-style profiles train brief knee entries and exits, not extended Muay Thai clinch systems.
sport_training_rules.then: teach punch_kick_knee chains, immediate knee from brief clinch, frame_exit, anti_clinch posture, and referee break awareness

sport_training_rules.rule: Muay Thai-specific clinch, elbow, sweep, and scoring assumptions are excluded unless the user selected Muay Thai or a cross-training context.
sport_training_rules.if: sport == kickboxing and rule_set not in [muay_thai_cross_training]
sport_training_rules.then: filter elbows, extended clinch rounds, dumps, and Muay Thai-only scoring language from kickboxing sessions
sport_training_rules.rationale: Muay Thai is related but not identical to WAKO or GLORY/K-1 kickboxing.

sport_training_rules.rule: Contact level must gate sparring recommendations.
sport_training_rules.then: do not prescribe hard sparring; use pads, bag, partner drills, technical sparring, and coach-supervised progressions

planning_rules.rule: Weekly phase allocation must mirror selected rule set.
planning_rules.then: point_fighting emphasizes speed entries; light_contact emphasizes controlled continuity; kick_light adds low-kick control; full_contact emphasizes above-waist punch-kick volume; low_kick emphasizes leg offense_defense; k1_glory emphasizes punch_kick_knee_damage_and_exits

planning_rules.rule: Competition week reduces fatigue while retaining tactical sharpness.
planning_rules.then: reduce hard sparring and heavy lower_body_strength; retain pads, movement, tactical drilling, mobility, activation, speed primers, and recovery

planning_rules.rule: Low-kick contact is a managed exposure, not a default volume target.
planning_rules.then: track shin, calf, knee, hip, adductor, ankle, and foot response; progress contact gradually; reduce volume after pain or poor mechanics

planning_rules.rule: Head contact requires conservative progression and stop conditions.
planning_rules.then: require coach oversight, lower total contact dose, recovery monitoring, symptom stop rules, and no hard sparring as default fitness work

planning_rules.rule: Recreational plans must not support aggressive weight cutting.
planning_rules.then: use gradual nutrition planning and refer competitive weight-making stress to coach_medical_supervision

planning_rules.rule: Fitness kickboxing keeps rule literacy but removes fight-contact assumptions.
planning_rules.then: program stance, guard, footwork, bag_pad mechanics, conditioning, and joint-safe volume without sparring, weight cutting, or competition tactics as required outputs

skill_assessments.assessment: Athlete identifies legal targets, contact level, clinch permissions, scoring incentive, and prohibited actions for selected rule set.
skill_assessments.pass_signal: Correctly explains 8 of 10 common situations without mixing Muay Thai, point fighting, full contact, low kick, or K1 assumptions.

skill_assessments.assessment: Point fighter scores controlled touch and exits without balance loss or counter exposure.
skill_assessments.pass_signal: Completes repeated entries with clean touch, guard recovery, and immediate reset under reaction constraints.

skill_assessments.assessment: Light contact athlete sustains continuous combinations with controlled power and defensive responsibility.
skill_assessments.pass_signal: Maintains balance, guard return, contact control, and breathing across multiple moderate rounds.

skill_assessments.assessment: Low-kick athlete can attack and defend legs safely.
skill_assessments.pass_signal: Shows low-kick setup, pivot, checking, step-out or pullback, return defense, and no knee or shin pain escalation.

skill_assessments.assessment: K1 athlete uses brief clinch knees without extended holding.
skill_assessments.pass_signal: Enters, lands or threatens legal knee, frames, exits, and resumes stance without long clinch wrestling.

skill_assessments.assessment: Athlete distinguishes clean damaging impact from low-effect or blocked volume.
skill_assessments.pass_signal: Chooses combinations that land cleanly, protects against counters, and explains round-winning criteria in scenario review.

skill_assessments.assessment: Athlete demonstrates safety prerequisites before increased sparring contact.
skill_assessments.pass_signal: Keeps stance, guard, defense, composure, stop-command compliance, and technical control under guided resistance.
